description: Implement the core pose detection engine using react-native-vision-camera with react-native-mediapipe for on-device pose landmark detection, and build the rep counting logic for all 8 exercises based on joint angle calculations.
steps: Add to package.json dependencies: 'react-native-vision-camera': '^3.6.4', 'react-native-mediapipe': '^0.3.0', 'react-native-worklets-core': '^0.4.0'. These are the community packages for on-device MediaPipe pose detection in React Native.

Create utils/poseDetection.js - Central module that exports: (1) POSE_LANDMARKS constant mapping landmark indices to body part names (nose=0, left_shoulder=11, right_shoulder=12, left_elbow=13, right_elbow=14, left_wrist=15, right_wrist=16, left_hip=23, right_hip=24, left_knee=25, right_knee=26, left_ankle=27, right_ankle=28), (2) calculateAngle(pointA, pointB, pointC) function that computes the angle at pointB given three {x, y} landmark points using Math.atan2, (3) calculateDistance(pointA, pointB) helper function.

Create utils/exerciseDetectors.js - Module with rep detection logic for each exercise. Each detector is a class/object with: exerciseId, detect(landmarks, previousState) -> {repCompleted: boolean, newState: object, feedback: string}. Implement detectors for: (1) SQUATS - track knee angle (hip-knee-ankle), rep counts when angle goes below 90 then back above 160. (2) PUSH_UPS - track elbow angle (shoulder-elbow-wrist), rep when angle goes below 90 then back above 160 while body is prone. (3) LUNGES - track front knee angle, rep when angle dips below 100 then returns above 150. (4) BICEP_CURLS - track elbow angle (shoulder-elbow-wrist), rep when angle goes below 50 then back above 140. (5) PLANK_HOLD - track body alignment (shoulder-hip-ankle angle near 180), count seconds held rather than reps. (6) SHOULDER_PRESS - track elbow angle with wrists above shoulders, rep when arms extend above head then return. (7) JUMPING_JACKS - track distance between ankles and wrists, rep when limbs spread and return. (8) DEADLIFTS - track hip angle (shoulder-hip-knee), rep when torso goes from upright to forward lean and back.

Create utils/exerciseConfig.js - Configuration for each exercise: { id, name, targetMuscles, difficulty, description, type: 'reps'|'hold', defaultSets: number, defaultReps: number, defaultHoldSeconds: number, landmarksUsed: string[], thresholds: {downAngle, upAngle} }. This is the single source of truth referenced by both ExerciseListScreen and the detection engine.

Update screens/WorkoutSessionScreen.js to integrate the camera and pose detection: (1) Import and use react-native-vision-camera's Camera component with the front camera and a frame processor, (2) Use react-native-mediapipe's usePoseDetection hook to process frames and get pose landmarks, (3) Pass landmarks to the appropriate exercise detector from utils/exerciseDetectors.js, (4) Maintain state for: currentReps, currentSet, sets (array of completed set data), isTracking, exerciseState (passed to detector), (5) Draw pose skeleton overlay on the camera feed using landmark positions (lines connecting joints), (6) Show real-time feedback text from detector (e.g., 'Go lower', 'Good form'), (7) Add 'Next Set' button that saves current rep count and resets for next set, (8) Add 'Finish Workout' button that navigates to WorkoutSummary with all set data.

Create components/PoseOverlay.js - A component that renders SVG lines/circles over the camera preview to visualize the detected skeleton. Takes landmarks array as prop, draws circles at each landmark and lines connecting: shoulders, elbows, wrists, hips, knees, ankles in a stick-figure pattern. Highlight the joints relevant to the current exercise in green when in correct position.
acceptance_criteria: utils/poseDetection.js exports calculateAngle and calculateDistance with correct trigonometry
utils/exerciseDetectors.js has working detection logic for all 8 exercises with state machine approach (up/down phases)
utils/exerciseConfig.js defines all 8 exercises with complete configuration
WorkoutSessionScreen uses react-native-vision-camera and react-native-mediapipe APIs correctly
PoseOverlay component renders skeleton visualization from landmark data
All files pass node --check syntax validation
Rep counting uses a state machine pattern (phase tracking) to avoid double-counting
